title: Finding Product-Market Fit with Superhuman's PMF Engine
description: Rahul Vohra shares the exact step-by-step engine Superhuman created to measure, optimize, and systematically increase product-market fit from 22% to 58%.
transcript_text:
Lenny: Welcome to Lenny's Podcast. Today my guest is Rahul Vohra, the founder and CEO of Superhuman. Rahul, product-market fit is often described as this mystical thing that you only know when you have it. But you took an engineer's approach and built a quantitative engine to measure and find PMF. How did that begin?

Rahul Vohra: Thanks Lenny. When we started Superhuman in 2015, I looked at existing definitions of product-market fit like Marc Andreessen's 'the customers are buying the product just as fast as you can make it.' That's a great lagging indicator, but it doesn't give you a leading metric or a roadmap when you don't yet have it.

Lenny: So what leading indicator did you discover?

Rahul Vohra: I came across Sean Ellis's benchmark. Sean had analyzed hundreds of startups and found that the single best predictor of product-market fit was asking users: 'How would you feel if you could no longer use the product?' with three options: Very disappointed, Somewhat disappointed, and Not disappointed. Sean found that companies that struggled to grow always had less than 40% of users say 'Very disappointed', while companies that grew sustainably almost always scored above 40%.

Lenny: And what did Superhuman score when you first ran the survey?

Rahul Vohra: We surveyed our early users in the summer of 2017 and our score was 22%. It was heartbreaking. But instead of despairing, we turned it into a four-step optimization engine.

Lenny: Walk us through the four steps of the PMF Engine.

Rahul Vohra: Step one is Segmenting to find your High-Expectation Customer (HXC). We looked only at the 22% who answered 'Very disappointed' and analyzed their job titles. They were founders, executives, investors, and managers who lived in their inboxes. We then took those personas and used them to filter out people who would never be great users.

Lenny: What about step two?

Rahul Vohra: Step two is analyzing feedback to convert on-the-fence users into fanatics. We asked users why they loved the product, and what was holding them back. We ignored the users who said 'Not disappointed'—trying to please them is a trap that dilutes your product. We also ignored the 'Somewhat disappointed' users who wanted things outside our core vision. Instead, we focused exclusively on the 'Somewhat disappointed' users for whom the main benefit of Superhuman resonated, but who were blocked by a specific missing feature like mobile search or calendar integrations.

Lenny: And steps three and four?

Rahul Vohra: Step three is building a roadmap that is 50% doubling down on what the 'Very disappointed' users love (speed, keyboard shortcuts, offline mode) and 50% fixing the blockers for the high-intent 'Somewhat disappointed' users. Step four is tracking the PMF score continuously over time. By executing this roadmap, our score jumped from 22% to 34%, and within six months it surpassed 58%.
